Chief Secy. Home Civil Sectt. Lko And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- R.B.S. Rathaur Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
It is alleged in the FIR that minor daughter of the informant has been enticed away by co-accused Shivam Saroj along with two unknown persons.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is not named in the FIR, nor in the statement given by the victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.,
the victim has not supported the prosecution at all, rather she has stated that after being annoyed with her parents, she went away from her home of her own accord and free will.

However, while giving statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has changed the prosecution story by making improvement and for the first time name of the applicant has been taken by the victim leveling allegation of rape.
The victim has refused to undergo for the medical examination.

It has been further submitted that there is contradictions in the statements of the victim under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and there is lack of corroborative evidence.
It is further submitted that the applicant is languishing is languishing in jail since 31.07.2023 without having any criminal antecedent.
There is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released from jail or tampering with the witnesses.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid facts as argued by the learned counsel for the applicant.

On due consideration to the contradictory statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.; refusal by the victim to undergo for the medical examination, coupled with the fact that the applicant is languishing is languishing in jail since 31.07.2023 without having any criminal antecedent and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Durgesh Saroj, involved in Case Crime/FIR No. 79/2023, under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n)/506/384 IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Sangramgarh,
District - Pratapgarh, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
